sources.entry: mcu-skills by Alex New - A collection of board-specific Claude Code skills for microcontrollers firmware development, one per board, covering STM32, ESP32, ESP8266, RP2040/RP2350, nRF52840 and AVR.Each skill documents pin mapping, clock and peripheral pitfalls, PlatformIO/toolchain setup and flashing.

summary.one_liner: A collection of board-specific Claude Code agent skills for microcontroller firmware work, with one skill per board covering STM32, ESP32, ESP8266, RP2040/RP2350, nRF52 and AVR boards.
summary.what_it_does: The repo holds about two dozen SKILL.md-based skills, each tied to one physical development board (for example WeAct Black Pill, Raspberry Pi Pico, Arduino Nano, or Waveshare ESP32-C6 boards). Each skill is meant to record board-specific knowledge such as pin mapping, clock and peripheral pitfalls, toolchain setup and flashing, so the model does not have to guess. Skills are organized by chip family directories (stm32, esp32, esp8266, rp2, nrf, avr, baikal). Each skill directory can include reference/ docs, a template/ project meant to build, and assets/ with board photos and pinout images. The README describes install scripts for macOS, Linux and Windows that symlink or copy a skill into ~/.claude/skills, and a plugin marketplace with one plugin per skill. It also includes a skill template, authoring docs, and validation scripts.
use_cases: Giving Claude Code board-specific context for STM32 firmware work
Getting correct pin mappings for ESP32 devkits
Setting up PlatformIO or toolchain builds for a specific MCU board
Flashing firmware to Raspberry Pi Pico or RP2350 boards
Avoiding clock and peripheral configuration mistakes on microcontrollers
Developing firmware for Arduino Nano or ATmega32U4 boards with an AI assistant
notable: One skill per specific board, not per chip family, with board-level pitfalls documented
Installable as a Claude Code plugin via a marketplace, one plugin per skill
Each skill includes a template project meant to build on real hardware
Covers a wide range of boards: STM32, ESP32 variants, ESP8266, RP2040/RP2350, nRF52840, AVR, and a Baikal BE-U1000 board
Includes a cross-chip ESP32 comparison file adapted from ESP32Features under CC BY 4.0
caveats: Each skill targets one specific board, so boards not listed are not covered
Install scripts are provided for macOS, Linux and Windows, but the README does not describe support beyond these
Vendored third-party code inside a skill's template/lib/ keeps its own license
